meta: Faucet or shutoff valve won't stop? We stop the leak and repair sinks, tubs and shower valves in Oakley, CA. Clear price first. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: Faucet and sink repair in Oakley, CA often begins with a valve that will not close or a drip that will not quit. We fix both, and we handle tub spouts, shower valves and outdoor spigots too.
Water you cannot shut off is the true emergency here, so that comes first below.
intro: Faucet repair means finding the worn part inside a tap, valve or fixture and replacing it, or replacing the whole fixture when the body is the problem. The usual culprits are a cartridge, a washer and seat, an O-ring or a supply line.

Diablo Water District supplies Oakley with water that averages 124 mg/L hardness, so mineral deposits are a common reason aerators clog and handles stiffen. The sections below cover shutoff emergencies, repair versus replacement, tub and shower valves, and what changes the price.

sections.h2: A valve or supply line will not shut off
paras: When a stop valve under the sink fails or a supply line splits, the water keeps coming until you cut it at the source. Our 24/7 emergency dispatch answers these calls at any hour, and the steps below buy you time.
do_now: Turn the other shutoff valves in the house first, such as the one under the sink or behind the toilet.
Close the main water valve, usually at the meter box or where the line enters the house, by turning it clockwise until firm.
Open the lowest faucet in the house to relieve pressure and drain the line.
Set a bucket under any active drip and lift stored items out of the cabinet.
Switch off power to anything near the water, such as a disposal or outlet in the cabinet.
If the main valve is stuck or leaks, call Diablo Water District at (925) 625-3798 for the street-side valve.

sections.h2: What is usually worn inside a dripping faucet
paras: A drip is almost always one small part, not the whole faucet. Knowing which part helps decide whether to repair or replace.

items.d: Single-handle kitchen and shower faucets use a cartridge that wears, sticks or lets water pass when closed.
Older two-handle taps seal on a rubber washer pressing against a metal seat, and either can pit.
Water at the base of the spout or a loose swivel often means a flattened ring.
Mineral flakes in the screen reduce flow and spray sideways, and cleaning usually fixes it.
Braided lines under the sink can kink or corrode at the nut and leak slowly into the cabinet.

sections.h2: Tub spouts, stripped knobs and shower valves
paras: Bathtub and shower valves hide behind the wall, so a stripped handle or a leaking stem can mean opening tile or an access panel. A stripped knob can sometimes be replaced alone, though a worn cartridge behind it should be changed at the same visit.

A showerhead that drips for hours after use points to a worn valve. A leak behind the wall shows up as a damp ceiling below, and a [[leak-detection|leak detection]] visit helps confirm the source before any demolition.

sections.h2: Repair, replace the fixture, or replace the valve
paras: The right call depends on the age of the parts, the finish and whether replacement parts exist. We say plainly when a repair will not last, and the table lays out the usual reasoning.

sections.h2: Tub and shower drains that back up
paras: A shower that drains slowly is usually hair and soap packed in the trap just under the tub. Clearing it with a snake often solves the problem, and we avoid harsh chemicals because they can damage older fittings.
If the tub and a nearby toilet or sink back up together, the clog is deeper. That job moves into [[drain-cleaning|drain cleaning]], where a camera shows what is in the line.

Hard freezes are uncommon in Oakley, but a cold snap can still crack an exposed spigot or the pipe behind it. A hose bib that drips when the hose is off, or sprays behind the handle, has a worn washer or a damaged body.
We replace spigots and add frost-proof or vacuum-breaker types when a homeowner wants one. Pairing the swap with a quick check of the line behind it is cheaper than a second visit later.

sections.h2: Why hardness matters for Oakley faucets
paras: Diablo Water District's 2025 report puts total hardness between 87 and 150 mg/L, with an average of 124 mg/L, or about 7 grains per gallon. That sits at the low end of the hard range, enough to leave white crust on aerators and shower heads. Soaking an aerator in vinegar often restores flow, and a [[water-softener-filtration|softener or filter]] reduces the scale at every tap.

Diablo Water District is responsible for the line up to the meter, and everything after it belongs to the owner. If water is bubbling between the street and the meter box, report it to the District before you pay a plumber for it. Replacement fixtures and shutoff valves are expected to meet the California Plumbing Code, which borrows its structure from the UPC.

sections.h2: What changes the price of a faucet repair
paras: Faucet work ranges from a ten-minute cartridge swap to a wall-valve replacement, so the price depends on what is actually wrong. Price comes first, once we have seen which part has failed.

factors.d: Premium and imported fixtures may need ordered parts, which affects timing.
Choosing a new faucet adds the fixture itself, and finishes vary widely.
Wall valves behind tile take longer than a stop valve under a sink.
Several faucets in one visit share the call-out and travel time.
Night and weekend emergencies are priced differently from scheduled visits.

sections.insurance: Insurers usually cover sudden and accidental water damage, such as a burst supply line flooding a cabinet, but not gradual drips from wear. Photograph the damage and keep the failed part, then ask your insurer before repairs begin.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 with the fixture type and what it is doing, and we will quote it before we begin.

faqs.q: Do you handle faucet and sink repair emergencies at night or on weekends in Oakley?
a: Yes. Dispatch runs 24/7, and a valve that will not shut off is treated as urgent at any hour.

faqs.q: What should I do when a valve will not shut off?
a: Close the main water valve for the house, then open the lowest faucet to drain the line. If the main valve fails, Diablo Water District's emergency number is (925) 625-3798.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace a leaking faucet?
a: Repair when the body is sound and parts exist. Replace it when the finish is worn, the body leaks or you have been fixing the same fixture again and again.

faqs.q: Can you fix a stripped tub handle?
a: Often the handle can be replaced without opening the wall, though the cartridge behind it may be worn too. We check the cartridge while the handle is off.

faqs.q: Can you winterize or replace outdoor faucets?
a: Yes. We replace damaged spigots, add frost-proof types and check the line behind them. Hard freezes are uncommon here, but a cold snap can still crack exposed pipe.

faqs.q: Do you repair premium or imported fixtures?
a: Usually, yes. Send the brand and model first, because some parts must be ordered and some finishes cannot be matched.

faqs.q: Is the water line before my meter my responsibility?
a: Everything past the meter, including every faucet and valve, is the owner's side. The District can tell you where its pipe ends at your address.
